full_judgment: 9. The question is whether after the death of the plaintiff this suit for permanent injunction could be continued by Khadem of the Darbarsharif. The deceased plaintiff himself has disowned the character of the wakf property and from averments in the pleadings it appears that he treated it as his personal property and his right to continue as Sajjadanashin was also a personal ground. As it has been mentioned that it is only in third generation of the family and the original founder was the grandfather of the deceased plaintiff. No custom had yet been built up worth the name because the Darbarsharif is not yet over 100 years standing. On the other band, it appears that after the death of the original founder his son Moulana Abdul Hye became the Sajjadanashin, and after his death the plaintiff became Sajjadanashin. Therefore, it can be assumed that the line is continued in the family and obviously that is the right to hold that the property is devolved upon the heirs of the deceased plaintiff i.e. defendants. The attempt on behalf of the respondent to be substituted as plaintiff is nothing but a device to deprive the members of the family of the office of the Darbarsharif. It is for the devotees to decide whom they would install as Khadem of the Darbarsharif but the stage has not yet come because after the death the respondent Madan Miah Chowdhury wanted to be substituted in the suit for permanent injunction. Right to sue does not survive after the death of the plaintiff because the suit was brought to establish personal right to office entitling him to possession of property. Suit abates on his death. In Ramsarup Das vs. Raeswar Das, AIR 1950 Patna 184 it was held that suit by plaintiff to establish personal right to office entitling him to possession of property abates on his death.
